messages:
julia: quick heads-up: i've been noodling on a 'token slimming' pattern to shrink our long-lived API key surface. idea: keep a very small set of long-lived admin keys, but mint short-lived intent tokens for most service-to-service and client flows. want quick feedback before i draft an RFC :wave:

mike: high-level +1. two quick Qs: runtime-derived claims (no mint call) vs minted ephemeral tokens. latency and cache invalidation are my concerns.

sarah: runtime derivation reduces mint pressure but we need a reliable, low-latency claim expansion cache. also TTL semantics are crucial: short TTLs reduce blast radius but increase mint frequency.

cory: minted ephemeral tokens are great for revocation & audit, but we add a minting infra surface (rate limits, auth for minting, retries). ops notes: must design for backpressure.

julia: thinking hybrid: router/edge attempts to mint ephemeral token for sensitive write paths. for low-risk read-only routes, allow a deterministic claim expansion path to avoid mint storms. minted tokens would include explicit intent claims so our policy engine sees the same attributes. :thumbsup:

alexa: must preserve lineage for billing and audit. encode original principal as `parent` claim in minted tokens or include `X-Orig-Actor` header at mint time. important: do not expose secrets in logs.

mike: agree, but guard metric cardinality. for telemetry labels prefer stable dimensions (org_id, project_id, principal_type) not token ids.

sarah: RBAC mapping: translate minted claims into existing role ids via static mapping in policy engine. avoid per-token dynamic role creation. keeps audits & policy evaluation simpler.

cory: what about external customer API keys embedded in apps? full ephemeral-only migration will break offline clients. we should support legacy keys during a migration window. approach: shadow-mint tokens when legacy keys used, emit deprecation telemetry, progressively tighten rate-limits.

julia: migration plan outline: 1) shadow-mint and log lineage for requests using legacy keys; 2) emit deprecation warnings in responses and dashboard; 3) progressively limit privileges and nudge SDK/clients to adopt auto-mint helpers. router accepts both during rollout.

alexa: pseudo-config for mapping rules (example):
```
# mapping rule example
match: project:proj-123:key:ABCD
mint_to: {sub: "svc:edge", aud: "inference", claims: ["read:dataset:proj-123"], exp: now + 900, parent: "user:alice@acme"}
```

mike: ensure SSO/audit pipelines can surface `parent` mapping. otherwise we lose who triggered the action.

sarah: enforcement: policy engine only consults `claims` and `aud`. `parent` must be explicitly documented as audit-only. include that in RFC.

cory: ops: mint service must be highly available and per-customer throttled. failure mode: if mint unavailable, fall back to cached derived-claims path for a very short grace period, else deny. define circuit-breaker behavior.

julia: agreed. fallback precedence: minted token -> cached deterministic claim -> deny. set strong SLOs for mint service; we should also plan canary rollout and health-weighted routing.

deploy-bot: canary rollout started: token-slimmer experiment on eng-sre canary group -> https://deploys.internal/redwood/rollouts/3322

alexa: next steps: i'll draft RFC sections: token shapes, claim vocabulary, migration timeline, metrics (shadow-mint rate, lineage-loss rate, cardinality), and ops SLOs. need owners.

julia: owners: julia (design + RFC lead), mike + sarah (policy & telemetry reviewers), cory (mint-service reliability), alexa (migration SDK/docs). target RFC ready in ~2 weeks (2026-04-04).

mike: i'll add notes about instrumentation and label design to avoid high-cardinality explosion.

sarah: i'll prepare policy examples and a mapping table for common roles and claims.

cory: i'll diagram failure modes and draft throttling defaults.

julia: thanks team. i'll open a draft tomorrow and ping reviewers. :rocket:
